purpose: FlywheelCaseIterator is a scripted Slicer module, adapted from SlicerCaseIterator, that iterates over NIfTI cases listed in a CSV exported from a Flywheel instance. It lets clinicians or researchers load images, edit segmentations in Slicer, and upload masks back to Flywheel.
summary: The catalog entry is well formed: the s4ext and CMake metadata agree, the listed Python files exist, the BSD-3 license permits distribution, and the source revision is "main". The code has real concerns. Module load runs an unconditional pip install of fw-pyqt-management. Connecting clears the whole MRML scene without a prompt. Closing a case deletes every volume and segmentation node in the scene, not just the case's own nodes. The API key is stored in plaintext, and downloaded patient images are cached under /tmp. I did not verify the pinned commit or run anything. The middle of CsvFWTableIterator.py was not read.

safety.rationale: No malicious or exfiltrating code was seen. Upload to Flywheel is the advertised function and is triggered by the user. Concerns are plaintext API-key persistence (CsvFWTableIterator.py lines 336-352), patient-image caching under /tmp (config_defaults.json lines 3-4), and an eval on stored state (line 954). Read lines covered about 60% of the file.

environment.rationale: FlywheelCaseIterator.py lines 41-42 pip-install fw-pyqt-management at module load with no user confirmation, and check_requirements(REQUIRED_MODULES) runs at import. This happens for every Slicer user with the extension installed, whether or not they open the module.

packaging.rationale: The CMake script list covers all five module Python files and the listed resources exist. EXTENSION_DEPENDS matches build_dependencies. The flywheel SDK import (CsvFWTableIterator.py line 34) is not declared anywhere, and TODO.md lines 57-59 acknowledge there is no version pin.

license.rationale: LICENSE.txt is a 3-clause BSD license with copyright Joost van Griethuysen, and the file headers match it. That permits distribution. Flywheel's modifications carry no separate terms, and the files state that Flywheel maintains them.

soundness.rationale: Connecting runs slicer.mrmlScene.Clear(0) with no prompt (line 378). closeCase's finally block removes all scalar-volume and segmentation nodes in the scene (lines 925-937). Both can destroy unsaved user work outside this extension's case. No tests are enabled.

utility.rationale: The README and docs/installation_and_usage.md give clear usage steps and a disclaimer. No sample data or runnable tests exist: the only test registration is commented out in FlywheelCaseIterator/Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt line 2. The Slicer extension index entry is tier 1 with a 'production' status in the s4ext file.

findings.title: Unconditional pip install of a dependency at module load, without user consent
findings.explanation: On import, the module runs slicer.util.pip_install("fw-pyqt-management") whenever the package is missing, then check_requirements(REQUIRED_MODULES) runs. Scripted modules are parsed at Slicer startup, so every user who installs the extension gets a package install, without being asked, at startup, whether or not they ever open the module. The install also pulls the package's own transitive dependencies into Slicer's shared Python environment. This is the kind of startup install the index policy asks to be removed or gated behind explicit confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Move the import and install into setup() (widget creation), ask the user to confirm the install, and keep pip installs out of module import. Also pin the version consistently with required_modules.json.

findings.title: Connecting to Flywheel wipes the whole MRML scene without warning
findings.evidence:
# Clear out any other instance's data from Slicer before proceeding.
slicer.mrmlScene.Clear(0)
findings.explanation: on_connect_api_pushed calls slicer.mrmlScene.Clear(0) before loading the batch table. Any unsaved volumes, segmentations, or other scene content the user has open are discarded. The user is not warned, and the clear happens right after an API key is entered, which is an easy action to take by accident. This is unintended data loss from user work, not a crash.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before clearing, or clear only nodes this extension created (for example by tracking node IDs or using the parameter node). Do not clear the entire scene.

findings.title: closeCase deletes every volume and segmentation node in the scene
findings.evidence:
# clean up any dangling volume nodes
            deque(
                map(
                    slicer.mrmlScene.RemoveNode,
                    slicer.util.getNodesByClass("vtkMRMLScalarVolumeNode"),
findings.explanation: The finally block of closeCase removes all vtkMRMLScalarVolumeNode and vtkMRMLSegmentationNode instances in the scene, not only the case's own nodes. A user who loaded an unrelated volume, or who is comparing a segmentation outside the batch, loses it on the next Next/Previous action or on Reset. Because closeCase runs in cleanup paths, this can happen even after an error elsewhere in the case.
findings.suggestion: Remove only nodes tracked in the case data (InputImage_ID, InputMask_ID, and the additional IDs). If an orphan sweep is needed, restrict it to nodes this extension created and tagged.

findings.title: eval() used on stored case state, inconsistent with ast.literal_eval elsewhere
findings.explanation: getCaseData calls eval() on the CaseData parameter string. The value is produced by SetParameter from a Python dict of Slicer node IDs, so the practical risk is low. eval is still unnecessary, and the same class uses ast.literal_eval at line 910. Any writer of that parameter, including a loaded scene file, could execute code during getCaseData.
findings.suggestion: Use ast.literal_eval as closeCase does, or store the case data as JSON with json.loads.

findings.title: Flywheel API key persisted in plaintext config file
findings.explanation: The API key entered in the GUI is written to the shared config at ~/.config/flywheel/fw_connect.json, and a key from the Flywheel CLI (~/.config/flywheel/user.json) is read and reused. The documentation says the key is saved for future use, but no secure storage or permission restriction is applied. Anyone who can read the user's home directory can use the key to access the Flywheel instance.
findings.suggestion: Use the OS keychain, or at least restrict the config file permissions. Document the plaintext storage clearly for users on shared machines.

findings.title: Downloaded patient images are cached persistently in /tmp
findings.explanation: Images downloaded from Flywheel are cached under CachePath/CacheDirName, which defaults to /tmp/flywheel_cache. On shared Linux or macOS machines /tmp is often readable by other local users, and nothing in the module clears the cache after the batch ends. TODO.md line 48 lists a cache-clearing option as unchecked. The exposure is of medical data at rest, and it depends on the Flywheel data's sensitivity.
findings.suggestion: Default the cache to a per-user, non-world-readable directory (for example the Slicer user cache or a tempfile.mkdtemp with 0700 permissions). Provide a cache clear action and clean up on batch end.

findings.title: User-controlled names are used directly in output filenames
findings.explanation: The reader name and the mask node name are concatenated into the output filename without sanitizing path separators. A reader name or segment name containing '/' or '..' can place the file outside the intended folder. The exposure is limited because the user typed the value, but it is an unvalidated path construction.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize reader and node names (for example, restrict to alphanumerics and a few safe characters) before forming paths, and confirm the resolved path stays inside the output directory.

findings.title: Flywheel SDK dependency is undeclared and unpinned
findings.evidence:
import flywheel
import qt
import slicer
findings.explanation: CsvFWTableIterator.py imports the flywheel SDK at module level, but required_modules.json declares only fw-pyqt-management 0.0.4. The project's own TODO.md (lines 57-59) notes that the required SDK version is not specified. Installs can therefore break on SDK API changes, and the dependency is not visible to the extension manager.
findings.suggestion: Declare the flywheel SDK and its version in required_modules.json, or in the install logic, and keep it consistent with the fw-pyqt-management pin.

findings.title: No active tests and no sample data
findings.explanation: The only test registration is commented out, so the extension ships without automated tests. Behavior of the batch iteration, mask save, and the scene-clear and node-removal paths is unverified in CI.
findings.suggestion: Add at least unit tests for the iterator logic (case index navigation, node cleanup scope) that run without a Flywheel instance.

not_checked: Commit e23ba0dff8db72a3283e38000c4d1130442aa31f and the scm_revision 'main' were not resolved or fetched; the source reviewed is only the content provided in the prompt plus the files I read.
CsvFWTableIterator.py lines 121-295, 400-515, 600-895, 990-1270, 1330-1410, and 1510-1530 were not read.
The fw_pyqt_management package (Config, FileItem._add_to_cache, check_requirements, check_developer_mode) was not available; its cache, config permissions, and install behavior are unverified.
The Flywheel Connect config and any other network calls, including the destinations of data sent to the Flywheel instance, were not traced beyond the SDK calls.
No CI results, build logs, or Slicer runtime tests were available, and nothing was executed.
The PNG icon and screenshot binaries were not inspected for content.
questions_for_author: Why is fw-pyqt-management installed at module import rather than in setup() after user action? Would you accept a confirmation prompt?
Is clearing the entire MRML scene on connect intended? Can it be limited to nodes this extension created?
Should closeCase remove only the nodes listed in the case data rather than every volume and segmentation in the scene?
Where is the cache directory cleaned up, and what permissions apply to /tmp/flywheel_cache on multi-user systems?
Which flywheel SDK version is required, and why is it not declared in required_modules.json?
